deck_context.source_summary: Class 17 follows the Java, OSGi and Resource API foundations from Class 16. It teaches how Sling Models adapt AEM context, receive values from explicit injectors, prepare a small view contract for HTL, delegate public Core Component behavior and optionally expose an eligible contract through Model Exporter.
deck_context.core_claim: A useful Sling Model makes its runtime inputs and optionality explicit, prepares a small stable view contract, delegates behavior it does not own and exposes JSON only when an exporter contract already exists.
canonical_facts: A Sling Model is created by adapting supported Sling context through the Models Adapter Factory.
Prefer a Resource adaptable when the model only needs resource content; use a request adaptable only for request-specific context.
Sling Model packages must be registered in bundle metadata for runtime discovery.
Injection is required by default unless optionality is explicitly declared.
Injector-specific annotations communicate the source better than generic @Inject.
Optional<T> is appropriate when absence is a legitimate part of the model contract.
Fallback precedence, normalization and derived values belong in the model rather than HTL.
HTL owns semantic markup and conditional rendering; the model owns prepared values and explicit state.
Core Component implementations are private and should be extended through delegation against public model contracts.
@Self with @Via(type = ResourceSuperType.class) obtains delegated behavior through the resource supertype.
Reusable queries, integrations and orchestration belong in an OSGi service; a model may inject such a service with @OSGiService.
An exporter-enabled model can be resolved by resource type and serialized for a .model.json request.
Not every Sling Model automatically exposes .model.json.

slides.title: A Sling Model turns AEM context into a view contract.
slides.intent: Establish the model's responsibility before introducing individual annotations.
key_points: Adapt supported AEM or Sling context.
Resolve inputs through the Models Adapter Factory and injectors.
Expose typed values and explicit state to HTL.
Optionally expose an eligible exporter contract.

layout.intent: Make the creation and consumption boundaries visible in one pass.

slides.title: The adaptable defines the context a model can use.
slides.intent: Teach developers to choose the narrowest context that supplies the model's real inputs.
key_points: Resource supplies properties, children and resource type.
A request adds bindings, attributes and request-specific objects.
Prefer Resource for content-only models.
Use a request only when request context is required.

local_context.required_background: Create a decision fork beginning with WHAT DOES THE MODEL NEED? Left branch CONTENT ONLY → Resource with ValueMap, child Resources and resource type. Right branch REQUEST CONTEXT → request adaptable with Sling bindings, request attributes and request objects. Show @ScriptVariable only on the request branch. Conclude CHOOSE THE NARROWEST ADAPTABLE.

layout.composition: Central decision question with asymmetric Resource and request branches, then a one-line decision rule.
layout.intent: Turn adaptable selection into a requirement-driven decision.

constraints: Do not imply a request is always required for HTL.
Keep @ScriptVariable on the request branch only.
Render Resource with an uppercase R.

slides.title: Model creation is a runtime contract.
slides.intent: Show that a compiled class is not automatically discoverable or adaptable as a Sling Model.
key_points: @Model declares the supported adaptable and resource type.
Bundle metadata registers model packages.
The adaptable and required injections must match at runtime.
ModelFactory exposes clearer creation failures than a null adaptation.

local_context.required_background: Use four numbered gates: 1 MODEL PACKAGE REGISTERED, 2 ADAPTABLE MATCHES, 3 RESOURCE TYPE APPLIES WHEN DECLARED, 4 REQUIRED INJECTIONS RESOLVE. Success produces MODEL INSTANCE. Failure rail: resource.adaptTo(GuideCard.class) → null; ModelFactory.createModel(...) → explicit exception/evidence. Do not show a full Java class.

layout.composition: Four serial runtime gates with success output above and a compact diagnostic comparison below.
layout.intent: Connect model discovery and adaptation to observable failure evidence.

visual_elements.main_visual: Registration and adaptation gate sequence with success/failure rails.

constraints: Render @Model, adaptTo and ModelFactory exactly.
Do not claim compilation registers a model automatically.
Do not imply resource type is mandatory for every model.

slides.title: Injection should name its source and optionality.
slides.intent: Make model dependencies readable and prevent silent ambiguity about their source.
key_points: Use source-specific injector annotations.
Injection is required by default.
Use Optional<T> when absence is legitimate.
Do not make every dependency optional.

Solid connectors mean REQUIRED BY DEFAULT; one dashed Optional<String> title means LEGITIMATELY OPTIONAL. Add warning: OPTIONAL EVERYWHERE HIDES BROKEN CONTRACTS.

layout.intent: Make source and optionality visible as parts of the model contract.

slides.title: Fallbacks and derived values belong in the model.
slides.intent: Move repository-specific decisions out of HTL while keeping behavior small and predictable.
key_points: Resolve configured, legacy and safe fallback values in order.
Normalize and derive presentation-ready values once.
Expose explicit empty state.
Keep getters deterministic and inexpensive.

local_context.required_background: Use a Guide Card title example. Input chain: title (configured) → heading (legacy compatibility) → Untitled guide (safe fallback). Then one preparation stage trims whitespace and derives getDisplayTitle(). Expose isEmpty() separately. Contrast MODEL with HTL: Java owns precedence and normalization; HTL receives displayTitle and empty and chooses semantic markup.

layout.intent: Show one concrete value moving from repository compatibility to a clean view contract.

constraints: Render title, heading, Untitled guide, getDisplayTitle() and isEmpty() exactly.

Do not add repository queries or service calls.

slides.title: The model owns data preparation; HTL owns markup.
slides.intent: Define a stable seam that keeps templates readable without turning the model into a rendering engine.
key_points: The model exposes typed values and explicit state.
HTL chooses elements, attributes and conditional markup.
Repository traversal and fallback precedence stay out of HTL.
Contextual escaping remains automatic.
